message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 292, "amount_cents": 2929}, {"order_id": 294, "amount_cents": 10248}, {"order_id": 295, "amount_cents": 9055}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to check the refunds table against the three refunds Alpha reported (orders 292, 294, 295). Listing refunds first.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 292, 294, 295 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list, so I'll fetch the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 40355 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Acme (40355) and birch (40935) are the only two customers I've checked so far, and both are returned by net_balance. The last customer in the orders list is cobalt, so I'll fetch its net balance next.
Refunds match Alpha's report, and all three customers (acme, birch, cobalt) have net balances. I'll record acme's payout of 40355 cents first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Refunds matched Alpha's report, so I'll record birch's payout of 40935 cents next.
Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's net balance of 25715 cents is the only payout left. Its orders (9909 + 27790) minus refunds (2929 + 9055) also give 25715, so I'll record it.
All three customers have been paid: acme, birch, and cobalt. The refunds table matched Alpha's report, so I'm finishing with the recorded payouts.
